title: Candidate self-scheduling: what it is and how to do it well
summary: Candidate self-scheduling lets candidates book their own interviews from real availability. What it is, why it cuts time-to-interview, and how to do it right.

faq.a: Overwhelmingly, yes. Booking a slot in a minute — often outside office hours, from a phone — beats a multi-day email negotiation. Candidates in active processes are usually juggling several employers; the company that is easiest to schedule with interviews first.

It should, and this is where basic booking links break. Proper self-scheduling intersects the availability of every required panelist, applies quorum rules for interviewer pools, and reserves the whole panel atomically at booking time.

faq.q: What stops a candidate from booking an inconvenient time?
faq.a: The offered slots are computed, not open-ended: working hours, buffers before and after interviews, daily interview caps per interviewer, and blackout dates are enforced before a time is ever shown to the candidate.
